name: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
authors: Shunyu Yao et al. (Princeton University; Google DeepMind)
reflection_type: search-guided | verbal-self-critique (LM self-evaluation of intermediate states used as a search heuristic, combined with BFS/DFS lookahead and backtracking)
feedback_source: self-generated (the LM itself evaluates/votes on partial states; no external tool, unit test, or trained verifier provides the heuristic). Note: the IO+Refine baseline uses groundtruth equation-correctness feedback, but ToT itself relies on self-generated value/vote signals.
iteration_structure: tree/MCTS-search (deliberate tree search via BFS or DFS over intermediate 'thought' nodes, with lookahead and backtracking)
reflection_object: reasoning chain — ToT reflects on and selects among intermediate reasoning steps ('thoughts', coherent units of text serving as steps toward a solution). The LM self-evaluates partial states (via value or vote prompts) to decide which branches to expand, prune, or backtrack from. No weights, prompts-as-artifacts, or persistent skills are modified; the object of deliberation is the in-context tree of partial solutions.
requires_training: none (uses off-the-shelf GPT-4 with prompting only; no fine-tuning or RL). The paper notes fine-tuning LMs in a ToT style is future work.
reward_or_critic_model: self-as-judge — the same LM provides the state-evaluation signal by either independently valuing each state (value prompt, e.g. classify a partial Game-of-24 state as sure/likely/impossible) or voting across states (vote prompt). No trained reward model or external verifier.
distillation_target: none — ToT performs inference-time search and does not distill the reflection into any persistent reusable artifact (no episodic memory, skill library, learned prompt, or weight update). Successor work (Chain of Preference Optimization) later distills ToT search trees into model weights, but that is outside this paper.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered — the deliberation/search behavior is entirely scaffold-engineered: a human designs the thought decomposition, generator, evaluator (value/vote), and the BFS/DFS search algorithm around an off-the-shelf LM. It is not an RL-emergent reflective behavior.
memory_type: short-term/scratchpad — the tree of partial solutions (states) is held in working memory during a single problem's search; no long-term or cross-episode memory store.
memory_persistence: within-episode — the search tree exists only while solving one problem instance and is discarded afterward; nothing persists across tasks or sessions.
memory_curation_mechanism: retrieval-gated / population-or-Pareto-selected (in-tree) — states are kept or discarded by the search policy: BFS keeps the best b states per step (breadth limit b, e.g. b=1 or b=5), DFS prunes states the LM deems impossible and backtracks; less promising branches are dropped to keep the frontier bounded. This is search-frontier pruning rather than a persistent memory store.
error_localization_granularity: step-level — evaluation, pruning, and backtracking operate at the level of individual intermediate thoughts/states (a step in the reasoning, e.g. one arithmetic operation in Game of 24 or one filled clue in Mini Crosswords), not holistic outcome-level scoring.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: intra-task — ToT explores and refines reasoning paths within a single task instance via search; it does not transfer learned experience across tasks or episodes (contrast Reflexion/ExpeL).
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: mid-trajectory-recovery — the search corrects in-flight by backtracking from dead-end/low-value states to a parent and exploring an alternative branch (explicitly shown important in the Mini Crosswords ablation: removing backtracking drops word-level success from 60% to 20%).
task_domains: QA/reasoning; math; creative writing / language generation (planning and search-heavy tasks). Specifically deductive/mathematical reasoning (Game of 24), creative writing with constraints, and lexical/constraint reasoning (crosswords).
benchmarks: Game of 24 (hard subset, games indexed 901-1000 from 4nums.com), Creative Writing (100 passages from 4 random sentences), Mini Crosswords (5x5, 20 games)
headline_result: On Game of 24 with GPT-4, ToT (BFS, breadth b=5) achieves 74% success vs 4.0% for chain-of-thought prompting (and 7.3% for IO, 9.0% for CoT-SC k=100); ToT at b=1 already reaches 45%.
baselines: IO (input-output) prompting, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting, CoT self-consistency (CoT-SC, k=100), IO+iterative-Refine (k=10, with groundtruth feedback), and best-of-100 sampling for IO/CoT. All on GPT-4.
gains_vs_baseline: Game of 24: ToT 74% vs CoT 4.0% (+70 pts), vs CoT-SC k=100 9.0% (+65 pts), and vs best-of-100 CoT 49% (+25 pts). Creative Writing: ToT preferred / higher coherence (the paper reports ToT generating more coherent passages than IO/CoT via GPT-4 and human evaluation). Mini Crosswords: ToT word-level success 60% and 4/20 games solved vs <16% word-level for IO/CoT; ablations: removing pruning drops to 41.5% word-level, removing backtracking drops to 20% word-level.
compute_cost_profile: Inference-only cost multiplier vs single-pass. Game of 24: ToT uses ~5.5k generate / 1.4k prompt tokens at ~$0.74 per case, comparable to ~100 CoT trials (CoT best-of-100 ~6.7k/2.2k tokens, $0.47) but with higher accuracy. Creative Writing: ToT uses ~5x the completion tokens/cost of IO/CoT (ToT ~4k/2.9k tokens, $0.32 vs IO $0.06). No training cost (no fine-tuning). Cost-performance tradeoff is tunable via breadth limit b.
known_limitations: Deliberate search may be unnecessary for tasks GPT-4 already solves (Appendix B.1); the work only studies three relatively simple tasks chosen to challenge GPT-4; ToT requires substantially more compute/API cost than sampling methods (mitigated by the tunable cost-performance tradeoff and open-source LMs); it uses an off-the-shelf LM with no fine-tuning, and ToT-style fine-tuning is left as future work; the self-evaluation heuristic need only be approximately helpful, implying it can be imperfect/noisy.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: self-verify — ToT's search heuristic comes from the LM self-evaluating its own intermediate states (value or vote prompts), with no oracle labels or external verifier required to run the method. (The compared IO+Refine baseline does use groundtruth correctness feedback, but ToT does not.) On Game of 24 the success/failure of a final equation is checkable, but the per-step value heuristic driving the search is self-generated.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive — across all three tasks ToT improves over IO/CoT/CoT-SC without using oracle labels for its search heuristic; gains are large (e.g. +70 pts on Game of 24) and ablations confirm the search components (pruning, backtracking) each contribute. Efficacy is somewhat task-dependent (designed for tasks needing exploration/lookahead; less useful where CoT already suffices).
calibration_effect: not-measured — the paper does not report confidence-calibration or 'reasoning-tax' effects; it focuses on task success rates rather than calibration of model confidence.
failure_attribution_capability: n/a — ToT is a problem-solving/search method, not a failure-attribution or error-taxonomy method. It does perform implicit step-level error localization via state pruning/backtracking, but does not classify failure modes or attribute blame.
failure_mode_addressed: Targets failure modes of token-level, left-to-right (no-backtracking) decoding: lack of exploration, no strategic lookahead, and inability to revise early pivotal decisions. Relative to MAST-style modes, it addresses premature/greedy commitment and absence of in-flight self-correction by enabling branch exploration, pruning of unpromising states, and backtracking from dead ends.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes — three task setups with all prompts released in the code repo (https://github.com/princeton-nlp/tree-of-thought-llm): Game of 24 (hard subset 901-1000 from 4nums.com), a 100-instance Creative Writing task, and a 20-game 5x5 Mini Crosswords task; these became commonly reused ToT evaluation tasks.
builds_on: Chain-of-Thought prompting (Wei et al., 2022); Self-Consistency / CoT-SC (Wang et al., 2022); Self-Refine / iterative refinement (Madaan et al., 2023); classical AI search and human problem-solving as search through combinatorial problem spaces (Newell, Shaw & Simon); ReAct (Yao et al., 2022, same lead author) for LM action/reasoning. Uses GPT-4 as the base LM.
extended_by_or_inspired: Chain of Preference Optimization (CPO, Zhang et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv:2406.09136) fine-tunes LLMs on ToT search trees to make CoT match ToT without the search cost; Graph of Thoughts (Besta et al., 2024); Language Agent Tree Search (LATS, Zhou et al., 2024) which combines ToT-style search with Reflexion-style reflection and MCTS; Tree-of-Thought-based program repair (Weng & Andrzejak, ISSREW 2023); broadly inspired the 'System 2'/deliberate-reasoning and inference-time tree-search line of work.
reasoning_model_native: no / not-native — ToT is a prompt-and-search scaffold around a non-reasoning base LM (GPT-4, 2023), not a reasoning model with built-in reflection like o1/R1. It is a precursor to the inference-time-search ideas that reasoning models later internalize; the paper itself does not target o1/R1-style models (which postdate it).
on_policy_distillation_link: Direct relevance via successor work: ToT search trees provide stepwise preference signal that Chain of Preference Optimization (CPO) distills into model weights (a form of search-to-policy distillation, DPO-style on ToT-derived preferences). ToT itself performs no distillation, but it is a natural source of on-policy search trajectories for distilling deliberate search into a single forward pass.
sample_efficiency: On Game of 24, one problem is solved with ~5.5k completion tokens (roughly the budget of ~100 CoT samples) yet outperforms best-of-100 CoT; search breadth b=1 already yields 45% and b=5 yields 74%. Creative Writing uses ~5x the tokens of a single CoT pass. So the reported gains are reached at roughly a 5x-100x inference-token multiplier vs a single pass, with no training samples required.
